title: Introduce RBACv2 policy compiler, service-principal KMS anchors, and audit fence
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: We need a deterministic, auditable translation layer from high-level RBACv2 policy declarations to operator-scoped bindings and KMS usage guards so that operator actions cannot circumvent residency and key-scoping controls. This PR introduces a policy compiler that validates and emits operator-scoped role bindings, a KMS anchor subsystem that binds CMKs to service-principal claim fingerprints, and an audit fence that normalizes outgoing audit headers and stamps provenance metadata. Changes include: (1) policy compiler that performs static validation (role inheritance, scope narrowing, region pin checks) and emits enforced bindings; (2) KMS anchor implementation that verifies CMK metadata (location, account, usage allowlist) and derives a short anchor fingerprint that is attached to operator credentials; (3) audit fence middleware that strips unsafe ephemeral headers, emits a canonical audit_provenance header, and records mapping between anchor fingerprints and effective bindings; (4) migration tool to validate existing tenant bindings and produce a safe report + suggested fixes; (5) feature flag gating (rbacv2_compiler_enabled) and a canary rollout plan. Testing & rollout: unit tests added for compiler rules and anchor verification; an e2e run in staging against a small set of tenant fixtures; a migration dry-run and presubmit report that ops can review. Checklist: [x] compiler core and rule engine; [x] KMS anchor verifier with region checks; [x] audit fence middleware and integration tests; [x] migration dry-run tool; [x] docs and operator runbook. Context: this work is driven by recent compliance reviews (SUP-1228) and a post-incident audit where operator-scoped bindings were inconsistent with KMS key locality. The compiler intentionally errs on the side of deny for ambiguous scopes to avoid silent residency downgrades. Backwards-compat: default behavior is off behind rbacv2_compiler_enabled; when enabled the compiler emits advisory hints before enforcement for 2 weeks, then flips to enforcement via rollout flag. Migration: run cmd/migrate/validate_rbac_bindings --dry-run against main to produce report. See docs/rbacv2/compiler.md for operator guidance.

Add static rule checks: scope narrowing, region pin validation, role inheritance tests
Implement KMS anchor verifier and anchor fingerprint generator (pkg/kms/anchor.go)
Audit fence middleware, canonical header format, and telemetry hooks
Migration tool for validating existing bindings and suggested remediations

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: "This looks good overall; please add a short section in compiler.md that explains how scope-narrowing decisions are computed and examples of ambiguous policies. Also add a fatal check to the migration tool when a binding would relax region pinning."

Priya Shah: "Can we add an explicit metric for anchor verification failures (pkg/kms) so SRE can page on unexpected KMS metadata drift? Also prefer context-aware logs rather than fmt.Printf in anchor.go."
Marco Diaz: "Audit fence is great. Two requests: ensure we keep original raw headers in the audit record (but not forwarded), and add a short retention note in the docs about provenance header TTL."

Asha Menon (author): "Addressed: added examples and deterministic tie-breaker logic in compiler.md; migration now fails fast when a migration would remove region pinning and emits remediation suggestions (see cmd/migrate changes); added metric anchor.verify.fail_count and switched to structured logging; audit fence keeps raw headers in folded audit blob (not forwarded)."
